RagShortTexts: The House of Wittelsbach held Bavaria and the Palatinate under the iconic blue-and-white.

Variants.Content: Bearing white-and-blue lozenges, the House of Wittelsbach entrenched its power across Bavaria and the Rhenish Palatinate. Splitting in 1255 into Upper Bavaria-Palatinate and Lower Bavaria under Dukes Louis II and Henry XIII, the dynasty held hereditary office as Counts Palatine, wielding paramount voting rights in imperial elections.
Historically loyal to the Hohenstaufen line, Duke Louis the Strict defended Alpine passes and Rhine river tolls against aggressive expansion by rival archbishops and foreign claimants.
Bavarian farms brew rich barley beer under customary land law. So long as dues in smoked hams and oats are delivered to ducal bailiffs, the valleys enjoy peace.
